headline: CharacterStrong social-emotional curriculum update, new bus behavior protocol, and cell phone policy presented by district staff
summary: Staff reported 2,256 hours of curriculum use this year, with 82% at the core Tier 1 level. Elementary schools aim for at least 5% of students to access Tier 2 supports by year end. Secondary schools aim for a 10% drop in behavioral referrals by the end of this school year. Early data shows 89 phone policy violations across secondary schools, involving 74 students, and a full update is set for November 24th.
discussion: Behavior screening: Questions covered how students are identified for extra support. Staff described SWIS behavior logs, the behavior response protocol, and a nine-indicator screener, and said research shows students with two or more referrals by October tend to keep getting more.

Cell phone policy effects: Staff said some schools have seen more social engagement, pointing to a school dance, and said a grant tied to pouch fees has been awarded but the funds have not arrived yet.

Parent involvement: Questions asked how families learn about behavior steps and the social-emotional curriculum. Staff said principals share the behavior protocol with families, and staff will follow up on whether the curriculum asks for parent involvement.

Secondary capacity: Staff said sustaining CharacterStrong depends on the time culture and climate coordinators have for training, and that the secondary network position may need to be restored in the future.

Bus behavior reporting: Drivers were trained last week on a new protocol. They report incidents on a form that goes to the transportation director and then to building administrators, who enter them into SWIS.
